title: Level the Towers by ±B
src: Media.net OA, IIT Patna (reported alongside the set above, from a screenshot).
body:
You are given the heights of n towers in an array A and a positive integer B. Every tower must change exactly once: either add B to its height or subtract B from it. Heights may become negative.

Return the smallest possible difference between the tallest and the shortest tower afterwards.

Function to complete

Complete minHeightDiff(A, B). It returns the minimum possible difference.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: First line: n. Second line: A[0..n-1]. Third line: B.
out: One integer: the minimum possible difference.
ref:
class Solution:
    def minHeightDiff(self, A: List[int], B: int) -> int:
        a = sorted(A)
        best = a[-1] - a[0]                 # everyone moves the same way
        for i in range(len(a) - 1):         # a[0..i] go up, a[i+1..] go down
            hi = max(a[i] + B, a[-1] - B)
            lo = min(a[0] + B, a[i + 1] - B)
            best = min(best, hi - lo)
        return best

wrong.why: skips splits that make a height negative (a common version of this problem forbids them, this one doesn't)
greedy: towers below the average go up, the rest go down

lc: GfG / InterviewBit: Minimize the Heights (related: LeetCode 910 Smallest Range II)

samples.ex: 1 + 6 = 7, 15 - 6 = 9, 10 - 6 = 4: the heights 7, 9, 4 differ by at most 5.
Moving both the same way keeps the gap at 2. Moving them apart only widens it.
